reason: Functional: the parent department's logo linking off-site to commerce.gov. The department name is the destination, which is what makes a brand name the right answer here.
Functional: opens notifications. The button carries its own text "Notifications" and the two sprite icons inside it have no alternative text of their own.
An avatar used as a link to the poster's profile, so a content image rather than a functional graphic, with no alt on the image. Same finding as the four in batch 06.
Functional: a back link to the collections index. The link's own text reads "Collections", the chevron is aria-hidden, and no alternative text was written for it.

Functional: a flag glyph marking the language of a translation, in a link whose own text reads "Russian". The empty alt is correct, because repeating the language name is exactly the redundancy the criteria warn about.
Functional: the masthead logo links to the university home page and the alt says so. Brand plus destination, the same shape as fi-2148 and fi-1627.
Functional: a div with role=button that opens the subscriber and account menu. The label names the action rather than the person glyph inside it.

Functional: the arrowhead logo links to the site root, with an empty alt because the link's own text reads "National Park Service". The redundancy filter applied the right way round, and the footer lockup on the same site, fi-5601, gets it wrong.
An avatar linking to the poster's profile, with no alt on the image. Same finding as fi-10994 and the batch 06 group.
Not functional: a story photograph in a headline link. The image has no alt attribute at all, so the announced name falls back to the link's title, which is the headline.

Functional, and the alt is good: an icon-only search submit button labelled with its action. Dropped as a duplicate of fi-2297, which is the same template with the same label on another page of the same site, and is already kept.

Functional: the footer lockup links to the site's own root. The alt is the agency and department name, which does not say the link goes home, and the sibling print-only image in the same link carries an empty alt.

Functional: a span with role=button that opens the site menu. The SVG title announces the noun "Menu", naming an area rather than what pressing it does, and the criteria ask for the action. Same call as fi-8777 on the same page.
Functional: an icon-only link to the newsletter signup, labelled by the link's title attribute. The text names the action and what is being subscribed to, with nothing about the envelope.
Not functional: a story photograph in a headline link. The alt repeats the headline, which is also the link's title, so it describes neither the image nor anything the headline does not already say.
Functional: the logo links to the site's own root. The alt is the programme name, with nothing to say the link goes home.
Functional: the close control of the mobile navigation. The alt names the action rather than the X drawing, and nothing adjacent repeats it.

Functional: a span with role=button that opens the account dropdown. "Account" names an area rather than what pressing it does, so a person cannot tell whether it signs them in, opens a panel, or navigates. Same call as fi-8775 on the same page.
Not functional: a story photograph in a headline link, with the headline repeated as its alt. Same finding as fi-10425 on the same site.

Functional, and the alt is good, the same newsletter link as fi-11123. Dropped as a duplicate: identical template and identical label on another page of the same site, so a second copy adds nothing for a human reviewer.
Not functional: a story photograph in a headline link, with the headline as its alt. Third instance of this template on lithub.com.

Functional: a bullet icon linking to the download page. The alt is the wiki page name, "TracDownload", run together as one word, while the title attribute beside it says "Download Trac". The better text is in the field nobody announces first.
Functional: the previous control of a carousel. The button carries its own hidden text "Previous" and the arrow has no alternative text of its own.

Not functional: a timeline graphic linking to a full-size copy of itself. The alt is the graphic's title, which is right for identifying it but gives a person no access to the twenty-two years of events it plots.
Functional: the live call to action. The link's label names the destination, the play glyph is aria-hidden, and the visible "Live" beside it is not what carries the name.
Not functional: a story photograph in a headline link, with the headline as its alt. Fourth instance of this template on lithub.com.

Functional: a role=button that toggles the site menu, holding both the open and close glyphs. The label names the action. The anchor has no href, which is a keyboard defect, but the image and alt pair is sound.

Functional: the wordmark links to the wiki's own MediaWiki page, so it is a linked logo. The alt is the bare project name, which on mediawiki.org tells a person nothing about where the link goes. The icon beside it is correctly aria-hidden.
Functional: the navbar logo links to the site root, and the link's title attribute even says "USDS Home". The alt is the initials plus "Logo", so what gets announced first names the image instead.
Functional: dismisses the promotional banner. The icon-only button is labelled with the action, which is all an X glyph needs.
